chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from one of them عليه السلام, who said:

If the traveler does not find water, then let him search as long as there remains time. Then if he fears that the time will pass him by, let him perform tayammum and pray at the end of the time. Then if he finds water, there is no qaḍāʾ upon him, and let him perform wudu (ablution) for what he is to face thereafter.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, required for wudu (ablution) when available
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: the traveler, the person in a state of travel addressed by the ruling
key_terms.فَلَا قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no qaḍāʾ upon him, meaning he does not need to repeat the prayer
key_terms.فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: let him perform tayammum, the dry ablution when water is unavailable
key_terms.وَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ: let him perform wudu (ablution) for later prayer when water is found

ai.seo_question: If a traveler performs tayammum because no water is available and later finds water, must he repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a traveler who cannot find water before salat (prayer). He should continue seeking water while time remains, then perform tayammum and pray near the end of the prayer time if he fears it will expire; if he later finds water, he does not repeat that prayer and should only perform wudu (ablution) for subsequent prayers.
